Examples: a screwdriver, a mixing bowl, a hammer, a computer. Distinct from HowToSupply, which is consumed during the process.

types.embedding_query_text: Tool: An instrument or application used to perform a task. Also called instrument, application, resource. Examples: heat tool.

chosen_type.label: HowToTool
chosen_type.justification: A heat tool is a tool used in a process.

candidates.label: HowToTool
candidates.comment: A HowToTool is a HowToItem that is used but not consumed when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result. Also called instrument, utensil, equipment. Examples: a screwdriver, a mixing bowl, a hammer, a computer. Distinct from HowToSupply, which is consumed during the process.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: UseAction
candidates.comment: The act of applying an object to its intended purpose or function. Also called utilize, employ, operate. Examples: using a tool to fix something, consuming food, wearing clothes.

candidates.label: MathSolver
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a tool or application capable of solving a subset of mathematical problems. Also called mathematical calculator, problem solver, equation solver. Examples: an online algebra solver, a geometry calculator, a calculus problem-solving app.

candidates.label: Review
candidates.comment: A critical assessment or evaluation of an item, such as a product, service, or creative work. Also called critique, appraisal, rating, feedback. Examples: a movie review on Rotten Tomatoes, a restaurant review on Yelp, a product review on Amazon, a book review in a newspaper.

types.embedding_query_text: Category: A class or group of items with shared characteristics. Also called class, group, set. Examples: over 40 sports.

chosen_type.label: Class
chosen_type.justification: Over 40 sports is a category, matching Class.

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

candidates.label: SizeGroupEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size groups used for various product categories. Also called size category, apparel size group, product size range. Examples: 'Adult', 'Kids', 'Petite', 'Plus Size'.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: WearableSizeGroupEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size groups or types for wearable products. Also called apparel size group, clothing size type, garment category. Examples: "men's", "women's", "children's", "unisex".

candidates.label: CategoryCode
candidates.comment: A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code. Examples: UNSPSC code for office supplies, NAICS code for manufacturing, a product category ID.

types.embedding_query_text: Data: Information collected for analysis or reference. Also called information, statistics, figures. Examples: local weather data.

chosen_type.label: Dataset
chosen_type.justification: Local weather data is a dataset.

candidates.label: Dataset
candidates.comment: A Dataset is a structured collection of information or data, typically organized for analysis or use. Also called data collection, data compilation, data repository. Examples: A spreadsheet of sales figures, a database of customer information, a collection of scientific measurements. Distinct from DataCatalog, which is a collection of multiple datasets.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: DataCatalog
candidates.comment: A DataCatalog is a collection or repository of datasets, often providing metadata and access information for each. Also called data repository, dataset collection, data portal. Examples: A government open data portal, a university research data catalog, a scientific data archive.

candidates.label: DataFeed
candidates.comment: A DataFeed is a continuous stream or single file of structured information, typically updated regularly, about one or more entities or topics. Also called RSS feed, Atom feed, data stream, information feed. Examples: A news RSS feed, a stock market data feed, a product inventory feed, a weather data API.

candidates.label: Observation
candidates.comment: An Observation is an intangible entity used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time, often quantitative. Also called measurement, data point, recorded value. Examples: a temperature reading, a stock price at a specific time, a survey response. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which is a specific type of observation with a numerical value and unit.

types.embedding_query_text: Policy: A course of action adopted by an organization or authority. Also called rule, regulation, measure. Examples: World Cup 2026 hydration breaks, hydration breaks.

chosen_type.label: Policy
chosen_type.definition: A course of action adopted by an organization or authority, such as hydration breaks.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class fits; hydration breaks are a policy, not an action.

candidates.label: DrinkAction
candidates.comment: DrinkAction is a ConsumeAction representing the act of swallowing liquids. Also called imbibing, sipping, quaffing. Examples: Drinking water, sipping coffee, consuming a soft drink, taking a shot of medicine.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: LeaveAction
candidates.comment: A LeaveAction is an interact action where an agent departs from an event or group. Also called depart action, exit action, withdraw action. Examples: leaving a meeting, exiting a social group, departing from a party. Distinct from JoinAction, which is its antonym, and UnRegisterAction, which implies unsubscribing from a service.

candidates.label: SuspendAction
candidates.comment: The act of momentarily pausing a device, application, or process. Also called pausing, halting, putting on hold, temporarily stopping. Examples: pausing music playback, suspending a computer process, pausing a timer.

candidates.label: DepartAction
candidates.comment: A move action representing the act of an agent leaving a specific location to travel towards a destination. Also called Leave, set off, embark, exit. Examples: A plane departing from an airport, a person leaving their home for work, a ship sailing from a port. Distinct from ArriveAction, which is the act of reaching a destination.

types.embedding_query_text: TimePoint: A specific moment in time. Also called specific time, point in time, moment. Examples: 22 minutes into each half.

chosen_type.label: Time
chosen_type.justification: 22 minutes into each half is a time point.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: InstantaneousEvent
candidates.comment: An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence. Examples: a computer log entry, a timestamp, a single click on a webpage. Distinct from Event, which typically has a duration.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: WeatherCondition: The state of the atmosphere at a particular time and place. Also called atmospheric condition, weather state, climatic condition. Examples: record temperatures, humidity, wind speed.

chosen_type.label: WeatherCondition
chosen_type.definition: The state of the atmosphere at a particular time and place, such as record temperatures, humidity, wind speed.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class fits; these are weather conditions, not medical conditions.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: ShippingConditions
candidates.comment: A structured value describing constraints and information about how a product can be shipped, potentially applying to specific product attributes. Also called shipping rules, delivery terms, freight conditions, shipping policy. Examples: free shipping for orders over $50, express shipping for lightweight items, international shipping restrictions.

candidates.label: MedicalConditionStage
candidates.comment: A medical intangible representing a specific stage of a medical condition. Also called disease stage, condition phase, severity level. Examples: "Stage IIIa cancer", "early-stage Alzheimer's", "acute phase of an infection".

candidates.label: FlightReservation
candidates.comment: A FlightReservation is a Reservation for air travel. Also called flight booking, airline reservation, plane ticket. Examples: A confirmed booking for a flight, a digital boarding pass, a reservation for a multi-leg journey. Distinct from Offer, which describes the availability of tickets for sale.

types.embedding_query_text: Season: A division of the year marked by weather patterns. Also called time of year, period, quarter. Examples: this summer.

chosen_type.label: Season
chosen_type.definition: A time of year, such as winter, characterized by particular weather conditions.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class fits; this summer is a season, not a media season.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: PodcastSeason
candidates.comment: A PodcastSeason is a CreativeWorkSeason representing a single season of a podcast, used when a podcast is structured into distinct seasons. Also called podcast series season. Examples: "Serial" Season 1, "Lore" Season 3, a specific season of a narrative podcast. Distinct from PodcastSeries, which is the entire podcast collection.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: TimeOfDay: A particular period during the day. Also called time, hour, part of the day. Examples: morning, evening.

chosen_type.label: Time
chosen_type.justification: Morning and evening are times of day.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

types.embedding_query_text: Temperature: The degree of hotness or coldness of something. Also called heat level, thermal reading, temperature reading. Examples: shaded air temperature.

chosen_type.label: Temperature
chosen_type.definition: A measure of heat or cold.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class fits; temperature is a quantity, not energy or rating.

candidates.label: Energy
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

candidates.label: EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an Enumeration of energy efficiency levels and certifications from various international standards. Also called energy rating, efficiency class, energy certification. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration, EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration.

candidates.label: Rating
candidates.comment: A Rating is an Intangible representing an evaluation on a numeric scale, such as 1 to 5 stars. Also called score, grade, review rating. Examples: a 4-star movie rating, a product's 8/10 score, a customer satisfaction rating of 5 out of 5, a restaurant's health inspection grade.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: CertificationStatusEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration defining the possible statuses of a certification. Also called certification state, approval status, credential status. Examples: Active, Inactive, Expired, Pending.

types.embedding_query_text: BodyPart: A part of the human body. Also called anatomical part, limb, organ. Examples: hands and forearms, arms, legs and torso, skin, muscles.

chosen_type.label: AnatomicalStructure
chosen_type.justification: Hands, forearms, skin, muscles, heart are anatomical structures.

candidates.label: AnatomicalStructure
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalStructure is a MedicalEntity representing any part of the human body, such as organs, tissues, or cells. Also called body part, biological structure, anatomical component. Examples: The heart, a bone, a muscle, a neuron, the liver. Distinct from AnatomicalSystem, which is a group of structures working together.

candidates.label: AnatomicalSystem
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalSystem is a MedicalEntity comprising a group of anatomical structures that function together to perform a specific task. Also called organ system, biological system, body system. Examples: The circulatory system, the digestive system, the nervous system, the skeletal system. Distinct from AnatomicalStructure, which is an individual part of the body.

candidates.label: SuperficialAnatomy
candidates.comment: Anatomical features observable by sight without dissection, including body form, proportions, and surface landmarks corresponding to deeper structures. Also called surface anatomy, external anatomy, visible body structures. Examples: the visible edges of the scapula, the cubital fossa for vein location, the contours of muscles under the skin.

candidates.label: Muscle
candidates.comment: A Muscle, as an AnatomicalStructure, is a contractile tissue that animals use to effect movement. Also called muscular tissue, skeletal muscle, smooth muscle. Examples: biceps, quadriceps, diaphragm, heart muscle. Distinct from Nerve, which transmits electrochemical impulses.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

types.embedding_query_text: PhysiologicalMeasure: A quantifiable indicator of body function. Also called biological measure, body metric, physiological indicator. Examples: core temperature at rest, sweat rate, blood plasma volume, body temperature.

chosen_type.label: VitalSign
chosen_type.justification: Core temperature, sweat rate, blood plasma volume, body temperature are vital signs.

candidates.label: VitalSign
candidates.comment: A measurable physiological function used to assess the most basic body functions and overall health. Also called physiological sign, health indicator, body function measure. Examples: body temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate.

candidates.label: BodyMeasurementTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: A MeasurementTypeEnumeration listing various dimensions of a person's body, often used for clothing fit. Also called body dimension type, clothing size measurement, anthropometric measurement. Examples: "Chest circumference", "Waist size", "Inseam length", "Shoe size".

candidates.label: BloodTest
candidates.comment: A MedicalTest performed on a patient's blood sample to diagnose or monitor health conditions. Also called blood analysis, blood panel, blood work. Examples: "A complete blood count (CBC)", "A cholesterol test", "A glucose tolerance test".

candidates.label: WearableMeasurementTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common measurement types used for wearable products. Also called wearable sizing type, apparel measurement, garment dimension. Examples: "chest circumference", "sleeve length", "inseam".

candidates.label: BioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".

types.embedding_query_text: Symptom: A physical or mental feature indicating a condition. Also called sign, indication, warning sign. Examples: dizziness, nausea, fatigue, palpitations.

chosen_type.label: MedicalSymptom
chosen_type.justification: Dizziness, nausea, fatigue, palpitations are symptoms.

candidates.label: MedicalSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical sign or symptom that is a subjective complaint sensed and expressed by the patient. Also called subjective symptom, patient complaint, reported feeling. Examples: "stomachache", "lower-back pain", "fatigue", "headache", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalSign, which is an objective finding.

candidates.label: MedicalSign
candidates.comment: A medical sign or symptom that is an objective physical manifestation of a medical condition, discoverable by diagnostic tests or physical examination. Also called objective symptom, clinical sign, diagnostic finding. Examples: "fever", "rash", "high blood pressure", "swelling". Distinct from MedicalSymptom, which is subjective and reported by the patient.

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: PreventionIndication
candidates.comment: A PreventionIndication is a MedicalIndication for preventing an underlying medical condition, symptom, or disease. Also called prophylactic indication, preventative use. Examples: a vaccine for measles prevention, a medication to prevent migraines, dietary changes to prevent heart disease, exercise to prevent diabetes.

candidates.label: DDxElement
candidates.comment: A DDxElement is an alternative, closely-related medical condition considered during differential diagnosis, along with the distinguishing signs. Also called differential diagnosis item, alternative diagnosis, rule-out condition. Examples: Considering "strep throat" as a DDxElement for a patient presenting with a sore throat and fever, alongside "common cold."

types.embedding_query_text: WeatherEvent: A specific occurrence of weather, such as a heatwave. Also called climatic event, weather occurrence, extreme weather event. Examples: heatwaves, heatwave.

chosen_type.label: Heatwave
chosen_type.definition: A period of abnormally hot weather, often lasting several days or weeks.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class fits; heatwaves are weather events, not delivery or sports events.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: BroadcastEvent
candidates.comment: A BroadcastEvent is a PublicationEvent representing an event that is transmitted over the air or online. Also called live broadcast, streamed event, televised event, radio broadcast. Examples: a live news report, a sports game broadcast, a concert livestream.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: FoodEvent
candidates.comment: A FoodEvent is an Event centered around food and drink. Also called culinary event, gastronomic event, food festival. Examples: A wine tasting, a cooking class, a food fair, a restaurant week promotion.

types.embedding_query_text: Activity: Something done for exercise or recreation. Also called exercise, physical activity, workout. Examples: physical activity, exercise.

chosen_type.label: PhysicalActivity
chosen_type.justification: Physical activity is an instance of PhysicalActivity.

candidates.label: ExerciseAction
candidates.comment: ExerciseAction is a PlayAction representing the act of participating in exertive activity to improve health and fitness. Also called working out, physical activity, training. Examples: Going for a run, lifting weights, practicing yoga, swimming laps.

candidates.label: PlayAction
candidates.comment: PlayAction is an Action involving playing, exercising, training, or performing for enjoyment, leisure, recreation, competition, or physical activity. Also called performing, engaging in recreation, exercising. Examples: playing a sport, performing music on stage, training for a marathon, engaging in a hobby. Distinct from ListenAction, which is consuming music; Distinct from WatchAction, which is consuming visual content.

candidates.label: PhysicalActivity
candidates.comment: PhysicalActivity, as a LifestyleModification, is any bodily activity that enhances or maintains physical fitness and overall health. Also called exercise, workout, physical exertion. Examples: running, swimming, yoga, weightlifting. Distinct from MedicalTherapy, which is a treatment for a specific condition.

candidates.label: ExerciseGym
candidates.comment: An ExerciseGym is a SportsActivityLocation that provides facilities for physical exercise. Also called gym, fitness center, health club. Examples: A local fitness gym, a CrossFit box, a university recreation center.

candidates.label: ExercisePlan
candidates.comment: An ExercisePlan is a CreativeWork representing a fitness-related activity designed for a specific health purpose, including routines or clinician-prescribed activities. Also called workout plan, fitness regimen, training program. Examples: A 30-day weight loss plan, a physical therapy exercise routine, a marathon training schedule, a yoga sequence.

types.embedding_query_text: HealthAspect: A dimension of health, such as long-term well-being. Also called health factor, wellness aspect, health dimension. Examples: long-term health.

chosen_type.label: HealthAspectEnumeration
chosen_type.justification: Long-term health is a health aspect.

candidates.label: HealthAspectEnumeration
candidates.comment: HealthAspectEnumeration is an enumeration of various aspects of health content, used to describe specific facets of health topics online. Also called health content categories, medical information facets, wellness topic types. Examples: 'Symptoms', 'Treatments', 'Causes', 'Prevention'.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: HealthTopicContent
candidates.comment: HealthTopicContent is web content about a specific aspect of a health topic, such as a medical condition, its symptoms, or treatments. Also called medical web content, health information article, wellness resource. Examples: an article explaining diabetes symptoms, a webpage detailing cancer treatments, a video on heart disease prevention.

candidates.label: HealthAndBeautyBusiness
candidates.comment: A HealthAndBeautyBusiness is a local business that provides services related to health and personal grooming. Also called wellness business, personal care service, aesthetic clinic. Examples: spa, gym, hair salon, nail salon, massage parlor.

candidates.label: HealthClub
candidates.comment: A HealthClub is a health and beauty local business providing facilities and services for physical fitness and wellness. Also called gym, fitness center, wellness club, athletic club. Examples: Gold's Gym, Planet Fitness, YMCA, a local yoga studio.

types.embedding_query_text: PhysiologicalStress: Strain on the body due to physical demands. Also called physical strain, body stress, thermal strain. Examples: thermal strain.

chosen_type.label: PhysiologicalStress
chosen_type.definition: Strain on the body due to physical demands, such as thermal strain.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class fits; thermal strain is a physiological stress, not a symptom or condition.

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: MedicalContraindication
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a condition or factor that serves as a reason to withhold a particular medical therapy. Also called contraindication, medical warning, therapy restriction. Examples: "pregnancy" for certain medications, "allergy to penicillin", "severe kidney disease".

candidates.label: VitalSign
candidates.comment: A measurable physiological function used to assess the most basic body functions and overall health. Also called physiological sign, health indicator, body function measure. Examples: body temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate.

types.embedding_query_text: BodyFluid: A liquid produced by the body, such as sweat. Also called perspiration, biological fluid, secretion. Examples: sweat.

chosen_type.label: BodyFluid
chosen_type.definition: A liquid produced by the body, such as sweat.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class fits; sweat is a body fluid, not a body of water.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

candidates.label: RiverBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A natural flowing watercourse, typically freshwater, flowing towards an ocean, sea, lake, or another river. Also called river, stream, waterway, current. Examples: the Nile River, the Amazon River, the Mississippi River, the Thames. Distinct from SeaBodyOfWater, which is a large expanse of saltwater.

candidates.label: SeaBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A large expanse of saltwater, typically part of an ocean or a large inland body of saltwater. Also called sea, ocean, marine body, saltwater expanse. Examples: the Mediterranean Sea, the Caribbean Sea, the Black Sea, the Caspian Sea. Distinct from RiverBodyOfWater, which is a flowing freshwater course.

candidates.label: Pond
candidates.comment: A Pond is a BodyOfWater, typically a small, still body of fresh water. Also called pool, small lake. Examples: a garden pond, a village pond, a duck pond, a natural depression filled with water.

candidates.label: OceanBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: An OceanBodyOfWater, as a BodyOfWater, is a large expanse of saltwater, such as the Pacific Ocean. Also called ocean, sea, marine body. Examples: Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Southern Ocean. Distinct from LakeBodyOfWater, which is an inland freshwater body.

types.embedding_query_text: PhysicalProcess: A natural process involving physical change. Also called physical change, natural process, evaporative process. Examples: evaporation.

chosen_type.label: PhysicalProcess
chosen_type.definition: A natural process involving physical change, such as evaporation.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class fits; evaporation is a physical process, not a medical procedure.

candidates.label: MedicalProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a process of care, invasive or non-invasive, used for diagnostic, therapeutic, preventive, or palliative purposes. Also called medical intervention, clinical procedure, healthcare process. Examples: "surgery", "biopsy", "vaccination", "physical therapy".

candidates.label: TherapeuticProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure specifically intended to treat a health condition or improve a patient's well-being. Also called medical treatment, therapy, healing procedure. Examples: chemotherapy, physical therapy, surgical removal of a tumor.

candidates.label: SurgicalProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure involving an incision with instruments, performed for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes. Also called surgery, operation, medical incision, surgical intervention. Examples: an appendectomy, a knee replacement surgery, a biopsy, a C-section.

candidates.label: PhysicalTherapy
candidates.comment: PhysicalTherapy, as a MedicalTherapy, is a process of progressive physical care and rehabilitation aimed at improving a health condition. Also called physiotherapy, PT, rehabilitation therapy. Examples: exercises to recover from a knee injury, post-stroke rehabilitation, back pain therapy. Distinct from OccupationalTherapy, which focuses on daily activities and functional skills.

candidates.label: MoveAction
candidates.comment: An action where a living agent, such as a person or organization, relocates to a different place. Also called relocate, transfer residence, change location. Examples: moving to a new city, a company relocating its headquarters, a person walking to another room. Distinct from TransferAction, where the subject being moved is an inanimate object.

types.embedding_query_text: PhysiologicalConcept: An abstract idea related to body function. Also called biological concept, physiological principle, body concept. Examples: heat buffer, biological limits.

chosen_type.label: PhysiologicalConcept
chosen_type.definition: An abstract idea related to body function, such as heat buffer or biological limits.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class fits; these are abstract concepts, not substances or structures.

candidates.label: ChemicalSubstance
candidates.comment: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.

candidates.label: AnatomicalSystem
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalSystem is a MedicalEntity comprising a group of anatomical structures that function together to perform a specific task. Also called organ system, biological system, body system. Examples: The circulatory system, the digestive system, the nervous system, the skeletal system. Distinct from AnatomicalStructure, which is an individual part of the body.

candidates.label: BioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".

candidates.label: AnatomicalStructure
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalStructure is a MedicalEntity representing any part of the human body, such as organs, tissues, or cells. Also called body part, biological structure, anatomical component. Examples: The heart, a bone, a muscle, a neuron, the liver. Distinct from AnatomicalSystem, which is a group of structures working together.

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

types.embedding_query_text: Group: A set of people sharing a characteristic. Also called category of people, class of individuals, population segment. Examples: elite athletes, recreational exercisers.

chosen_type.label: StatisticalPopulation
chosen_type.justification: Elite athletes and recreational exercisers are statistical populations.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: SizeGroupEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size groups used for various product categories. Also called size category, apparel size group, product size range. Examples: 'Adult', 'Kids', 'Petite', 'Plus Size'.

candidates.label: WearableSizeGroupEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size groups or types for wearable products. Also called apparel size group, clothing size type, garment category. Examples: "men's", "women's", "children's", "unisex".

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.
